races.title: State Senate, District 40
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Kristie Bruce-Lane
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California State Senate District 40. Holds bachelor's degrees in nutritional science and crop science from Cal Poly San Luis Obispo (1997). Worked in healthcare and agriculture, and was elected in 2020 to the Olivenhain Municipal Water District board. Ran for Assembly District 76 in 2022 and 2024.

endorsements.text: Reform California endorsed her in the 2026 race, according to Ballotpedia's list of endorsements and voter-guide recommendations.
The Republican Party of California endorsed her in 2024 for Assembly District 76.

cands.gaps: We could not find where she was born or raised, or when she came to California. We found no 2026 campaign platform statements, since she did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 survey, and nothing on her positions on data centers, development, H-1B, guns, abortion, school choice or foreign land ownership. Her stated positions come from a 2022 survey only. We found no news reporting on her and no documented controversies or foreign ties. Her job history is described only in general terms, with no employers, dates or titles given for her healthcare and agriculture careers.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Elected director (later vice president) of the Olivenhain Municipal Water District since 2020; previous private-sector careers in healthcare and agriculture; described as a businesswoman; founder of a foundation. Ran for the Assembly in 2022 and 2024 without winning.
qual.why: A local elected office plus business and private-sector experience fits the middle band. She has held no legislative seat and has no documented law, policy or budget career.
qual.label: A local elected office plus business and private-sector experience fits the middle band. She has held no legislative seat and has no documented law, policy or budget career.

back-police-order.evidence: In her 2022 Ballotpedia survey she said public safety is a priority, that reclassifying felonies as misdemeanors has contributed to soaring crime, and that she supports law enforcement and crime victims.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: In her 2022 Ballotpedia survey she said she knows taxes are too high. She named no specific property-tax proposal.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 2 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 2 only promised

cands.name: Mara Elliott
cands.bio: Lawyer and Democrat who served as elected San Diego City Attorney from 2016 to 2024, the first woman and first Latina in that job. She earned her law degree at McGeorge School of Law. She is the Democratic nominee for California State Senate District 40 in 2026.

endorsements.text: Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions (AFL-CIO), California Nurses Association, California Teachers Association, and Equality California are among the endorsements Ballotpedia lists for her 2026 campaign.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Elliott was born or raised, or when she moved to California. We found no stated position or documented action from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, growth and land protection, H-1B or immigration enforcement, school choice or teacher pay. Her gun and reproductive-healthcare items come from her own campaign survey, not from records of specific bills or rulings. We also did not find her specific statements as City Attorney on policing pay or pensions.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Lawyer who worked under former San Diego City Attorney Jan Goldsmith, then served two terms as elected San Diego City Attorney (2016-2024). She advised the City Council and mayor, including on the extent of the mayor's power over the city budget, and ran the office's conservatorship and civil enforcement units.
qual.why: Eight years in local elected office plus a legal career in public law places her in the middle-to-upper part of the range. She has no record of service in a legislature itself.
qual.label: Eight years in local elected office plus a legal career in public law places her in the middle-to-upper part of the range. She has no record of service in a legislature itself.

second-amendment.evidence: As City Attorney she worked with law enforcement and courts on San Diego's gun violence prevention approach and helped train more than 500 California law enforcement agencies on gun violence restraining orders (red-flag orders), according to her own Ballotpedia survey answers.

pro-life.evidence: She listed protecting access to lifesaving healthcare, including reproductive healthcare, as a campaign priority.

back-police-order.evidence: She says she will partner with law enforcement on behavioral health support and school safety, and secure resources to implement Prop 36.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 3 priorities; 1 backed by their record, 1 only promised
